title: The did:webvh log watch stats its files once per sync turn; use inotify
description:
`[did_webvh].log_file` and `witness_file` are watched by comparing their
length and modification time once per turn of the sync loop
(`crates/mimid-agent/src/didwebvh.rs`, `LogWatch::check`, run as
`BeforeSync`). The module's own Limitations say so: "The watch polls on
the sync interval".

Mark 2026-11-27: "i dont like poll loops"; "we spent 50 years putting
events in *nix. use it".

## What it costs now

- A controller that writes the log waits up to one sync interval for the
  agent to notice, for no reason: the kernel knew at the write.
- Every turn of the sync loop stats two files whether or not anything
  changed.
- A write in place can be read half-written, which is refused and taken
  at the next change (already documented).

## What to do

Watch the files with inotify (`IN_CLOSE_WRITE`, `IN_MOVED_TO`) and wake
the sync loop on an event, keeping the stat-and-digest comparison as the
check that the contents really changed. The `notify` crate wraps this
per platform; mimid supports Linux, so raw `inotify` is also an option
and is one fewer dependency.

Keep the turn-by-turn look as a fallback, not as the mechanism: a watch
can be lost (the file replaced, the directory moved, the queue
overflowed with `IN_Q_OVERFLOW`), and a watch that silently stopped
working is worse than a slow one. On overflow or error, re-add the watch
and compare at once.

## Where it is written down

The Limitations list in `crates/mimid-agent/src/didwebvh.rs` says the
watch polls. That line is the claim this bead changes, so it changes in
the same commit.
